articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got social-engineered harder than a freshman at DEF CON, leading to the Obama White House Instagram getting draped in pro-Iranian propaganda. When your chatbot has worse OPSEC than a drunk politician's Twitter account, maybe it's time to rethink automation.

articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: A CISA contractor decided to open-source the government's crown jewels by dumping AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's their personal dotfiles repo. Nothing says 'cybersecurity leadership' like accidentally giving everyone root access to federal infrastructure.

articles.title: Malicious Notifications Could Trick Google Gemini Users
articles.summary: Cops are using license plate readers for everything from school enrollment checks to noise complaints because apparently warrants are just suggestions now. Mission creep meets surveillance state: coming soon to a dystopia near you.

articles.title: Philly Cops Admit That They’re Tracking “First Amendment Activity” Critical of AI
articles.summary: The Pentagon's running an AI propaganda mill targeting Latin America, mixing personal finance tips with military cheerleading like some demented financial advisor with an imperialism fetish. Psyops disguised as lifestyle content—how very 2025.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philly cops are tracking 'First Amendment activity' critical of AI data centers because apparently exercising constitutional rights is now suspicious behavior. The surveillance state really said 'hold my beer' to the whole democracy thing.

articles.title: UK banks offered access to OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 amid exclusion from Anthropic’s Glasswing expansion
articles.summary: Another bug hunter said 'fuck responsible disclosure' and leaked Microsoft exploits after Redmond's typical corporate stonewalling routine. When the disclosure process is more broken than the vulnerabilities, maybe the problem isn't the researchers.

articles.title: Shrinking the IAM Attack Surface through Identity Visibility and Intelligence Platforms (IVIP)
articles.summary: VS Code's one-click GitHub token theft attack proves that developer tools are basically malware with better branding. Click a link, lose your repos—it's like phishing but with more JavaScript and existential dread.

articles.title: New HTTP/2 Bomb Vulnerability Allows Remote DoS on NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy & Cloudflare
articles.summary: Windows Search URI vulnerability lets attackers steal NTLMv2 hashes because Microsoft's approach to security is apparently 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it, and if it is broke, also don't fix it.' Classic Redmond energy.

articles.summary: HTTP/2 Bomb vulnerability can DoS major web servers including NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, and Cloudflare because apparently the internet's backbone is held together with digital duct tape. When everyone's vulnerable, no one is safe.

articles.title: Tuskira Quell identifies, mitigates, and validates zero-day risk before breach
articles.summary: Microsoft backed down from legal threats against security researchers after the community collectively told them to touch grass. Nothing like the fear of looking like corporate bullies to make lawyers suddenly discover the value of responsible disclosure.
